story.title: Google Introduces Selfie Video Sign-In Feature for Account Access
story.summary: Google has launched a new feature that allows users to sign in to their accounts using a selfie video. This option is designed to help users log in or recover their accounts if they forget their passwords or cannot access their preferred devices.

explore_lenses.label: Who can use it, and when?
explore_lenses.title: It is a pre-set recovery option, not a lockout fix
explore_lenses.summary: The selfie video must be enrolled before a user loses access, and availability is limited by region, account type and device. It supplements rather than replaces Google’s other recovery methods.

claims.text: Google says selfie video is not available for all regions, accounts or devices, and users must have previously set one up to use it in account recovery.
Users cannot add a selfie video while locked out or already in the account-recovery process.
Google Workspace accounts, child accounts and accounts enrolled in the Advanced Protection Program are currently excluded from adding selfie videos.
Google frames the feature as another option alongside passkeys and recovery contacts, rather than a replacement for them.

explore_lenses.label: What biometric data does Google keep?
explore_lenses.title: Deletion and optional reuse have limits
explore_lenses.summary: Google says the enrollment video is encrypted, can be deleted, and is normally for sign-in. Its support documentation also describes optional reuse of video and related data to improve verification systems, plus circumstances in which deletion is not immediate.

claims.text: Google says the sign-in selfie video is stored with consent, encrypted at rest and used for sign-in unless the user opts in to additional purposes.

Google’s help page says users can opt in to let Google use the video and related data to improve facial recognition, age estimation and other verification methods, and can later revoke that permission.
After a user deletes a selfie video, Google says it may retain it temporarily as a security measure; it may retain it longer when it says this is needed to enforce a Google policy violation.
Deleting the video removes the ability to use that stored video for sign-in recovery.

explore_lenses.label: Can it withstand deepfakes and impersonation?
explore_lenses.title: Google uses liveness checks, but offers no public rates
explore_lenses.summary: The system compares a new video with the prior enrollment video and asks for movements intended to show that the recording is live. Google presents this as a defense against fake photos, videos and deepfakes, but has not published performance measurements in the materials consulted.

claims.text: During recovery, Google says it may ask the user to make a short face video with a required action such as turning their head, then compare it with the saved video to verify identity.
Google says it combines saved-video matching, movement-based liveness checks and its standard suspicious-sign-in defenses to counter impersonation attempts including deepfakes.
Google advises people whose appearance changes significantly to update their saved selfie video, indicating that matching relies on continuity between the stored and new recordings.

related_stories.title: Wildfire Forces Evacuation of Nearly 12,000 Tourists in Southwest France
related_stories.summary: A wildfire in Le Porge, southwest France, has led to the evacuation of nearly 12,000 people, primarily tourists. The fire, which began around midday on Wednesday, has prompted a significant response from hundreds of firefighters battling the flames. The region has been experiencing extreme heat, contributing to the wildfire's rapid spread.

related_stories.title: France Evacuates 20,000 Amid Wildfires in Southwestern Region
related_stories.summary: Approximately 20,000 people have been evacuated from towns and holiday resorts in southwestern France due to a raging wildfire near the coastal town of Lege Cap-Ferret. Most of those evacuated were tourists from campsites around Arcachon Bay in the Gironde region.

related_stories.title: FDA Advisory Committee Reviews Peptide Accessibility and Safety
related_stories.summary: An FDA advisory committee is convening to evaluate the accessibility and safety of over six peptides that have gained popularity as wellness treatments. Critics highlight the lack of sufficient data on their efficacy and safety, raising concerns about their promotion by influencers. The discussions aim to determine whether to ease restrictions on these substances.

related_stories.title: Houthi Attacks on Saudi Tankers Raise Oil Price Concerns
related_stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels, backed by Iran, have attacked two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, raising concerns about the future of oil and gas prices. This incident may represent a new front in the ongoing conflict involving the US and Iran, prompting discussions on its potential economic impact, particularly on gas prices in the United States.
